item.title: Hedge Funds Dial Up Bearish Kiwi Bets to Record on Oil Rebound
item.description: Leveraged funds have taken their short positions on the New Zealand dollar to a record high, betting that a recent rebound in global oil prices may exacerbate domestic economic pressures.

item.title: India Private Banks See Corporate Loans Rise as Bond Yields Climb
item.description: Managements sounded fairly confident that credit demand will hold up.

item.title: Soybeans and Corn Extend Gains as US-Iran Hostilities Escalate
item.description: Soybeans and corn futures extended gains as crude oil jumped after hostilities in the Middle East escalated, boosting the appeal of biofuels.

item.title: Chinese Traders Unwind Leveraged Bets at Fastest Pace Since 2016
item.description: Chinese stock traders unwound leveraged positions at the fastest pace since the 2015–2016 market crash on Friday, as fears that the AI-driven rally had become overstretched triggered a global equities rout.

item.title: Innolight Gauges Interest for $8 Billion Hong Kong Listing
item.description: China’s Zhongji Innolight Co. is starting to gauge investor demand for its Hong Kong listing, according to terms of the deal seen by Bloomberg News, bringing it a step closer to what may be the city’s largest first-time share sale in seven years.

item.title: Moutai Hikes Price of Flagship Liquor for Second Time in Months
item.description: Kweichow Moutai Co. raised prices of its flagship Feitian Moutai spirit for the second time in several months, as China’s biggest liquor maker works to boost margins hit by sagging demand.

item.title: Tungsten Miner’s Stock Jumps as Billionaire Forrest Buys Stake
item.description: EQ Resources Ltd. shares surged after mining billionaire Andrew Forrest agreed to acquire a 16.8% stake in the Sydney-listed tungsten producer from Oaktree Capital Management LP.

item.title: US, Congo Ebola Travel Restrictions May Hamper Humanitarian Aid Response
item.description: New US and Congolese travel restrictions aimed at keeping Ebola from spreading across borders are drawing warnings from aid organizations and medical experts who say the measures could undermine efforts to control the world’s fastest-growing outbreak of the virus.

item.title: INR/USD: HSBC Offers Indian Diaspora 19x Leverage on FCNR(B) Deposits
item.description: When Moumita Shome landed in Dubai from Australia last month, the calls from bankers started almost immediately.

item.title: Traders Cut Taiwan Stock Leverage at Fastest Pace in 15 Months
item.description: Taiwan’s retail investors unwound their leveraged stock bets at the fastest pace since April 2025 on Friday, helping drive the local equity market into a technical correction.

item.title: Chinese Stocks Rebound After National Team Reveals Buying
item.description: Chinese shares rose following last week’s rout, after two major state funds revealed fresh purchases and as regulators are set to meet with key industry participants.

item.title: Venezuela’s Official Death Toll From Twin Quakes Rises to 5,208
item.description: Venezuela’s official death toll from the twin earthquakes that struck the country on June 24 rose to 5,208, according to the latest figures released on Sunday by National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez.

item.title: IDR/USD: Rupiah May Recover on Rate Hike, Stronger Fiscals, Analysts Say
item.description: The Indonesian rupiah is poised for a period of stability, with analysts expecting the central bank to continue supporting Asia’s worst-performing currency and foreign funds to step up purchases of the nation’s high-yielding bonds.

item.title: Gold Steadies as Traders Assess Rates Path After US-Iran Clashes
item.description: Gold steadied after the US and Iran ramped up attacks over the weekend, as traders assess the likelihood of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates to contain inflation.

item.title: The Brewing Battle Between Netflix and YouTube Over Creators
item.description: Netflix is doing deals with many of YouTube’s biggest stars. How will YouTube respond?

item.title: TSMC’s $265 Billion US Spend Driven by Demand, Rivals, CFO Says
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is adding $100 billion to its investments in Arizona to meet strong demand from US customers and to ward off ambitious rivals, a senior executive said this week.

item.title: Teleperformance Wants Entire BPO Staff to Be AI-Enabled by 2027
item.description: French business process outsourcing company Teleperformance SE plans to embed artificial intelligence in the workflow of its entire workforce of half-a-million people, speeding up adoption of the same technology that’s driving labor market disruption for the industry.

item.title: Oil Climbs as Middle East Conflict Escalates: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil gained in early trading after US and Iran attacks escalated over the weekend, adding further pressure on Asian markets already rattled by a slump in chip stocks.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 20
item.description: Brent crude jumped after the US and Iran escalated hostilities, including the targeting of vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz and an attack on a key oil facility in Kuwait over the weekend.

item.title: Korea President’s Stock Dream Bumps Into Leveraged ETF Backlash
item.description: South Korea’s most closely watched stock-market innovation is morphing into a headache for President Lee Jae Myung.

item.title: Aussie’s Slide Versus Kiwi to Slow on Rate Gap, Strategists Say
item.description: The Australian dollar’s steep selloff against its New Zealand counterpart is set to slow, with analysts saying Australia’s higher interest rates and a key technical support will cushion the currency.

item.title: Bond Traders Take Warsh at Word, See Inflation Fight Continuing
item.description: Bond traders and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh are in agreement on a crucial point: The central bank’s fight against inflation still seems far from over.

item.title: Tropical Storm Watches Posted Across Florida’s Panhandle Region
item.description: A tropical storm watch has been issued for the Florida Panhandle as the Atlantic’s next event takes shape off shore.

item.title: Extreme Stock Swings Tempt Funds Into Reverse Dispersion Trade
item.description: Betting that individual stocks will be volatile while the S&P 500 stays relatively calm has been a popular and successful hedge fund strategy. But with the swings in share prices reaching extreme levels, the reverse trade is gaining traction with investors.

item.title: Prediction Markets Swell to 27% of Sports Bets During World Cup
item.description: Prediction-market trading has surged during a blowout World Cup, far outpacing the growth at traditional sportsbooks and driving home the competitive threat that companies like Kalshi now pose to the sports-gambling industry.

item.title: Big Tech Needs to Justify AI Spending as Investors Dump Stocks
item.description: After last week’s wipeout in chips and the broader selloff in technology stocks, pressure is building for the biggest spenders on artificial intelligence to justify their expenditures to beleaguered traders with increasingly itchy fingers hovering over their sell buttons.

item.title: Safest Carry in Emerging Markets Is in Latin American Currencies
item.description: Emerging-market currency volatility has dropped to the lowest since the start of year and that’s re-energizing carry trades, particularly those involving Latin America that are seen to offer the juiciest returns.

item.title: Clear Skies Now Expected for World Cup Final in New Jersey
item.description: Clear skies are expected across northern New Jersey as the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain is set to get underway at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon with about 80,000 fans on hand.

item.title: Alibaba’s Qwen Unveils Preview of Flagship AI Model
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. launched a preview version of its flagship Qwen3.8 Max model, which it described as comparable to leading frontier AI models and second only to Anthropic PBC’s Fable 5.
